Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap from today’s discovery and proposed next steps so we can get you a prescriptive recommendation between Redwood Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity (and if relevant, Private VPC).

Recap of what you shared:
- Primary product: real-time fraud scoring API for customer transactions.
- Typical traffic: steady baseline ~120 rps; spikes to ~450 rps during peak events.
- Latency targets: p95 end-to-end scoring under 50ms; p99 ideally under 120ms.
- Model: 7B reranking model for candidate scoring with short context (~64 tokens).
- Security: SOC2 + vendor review coming from procurement (Priya).

Key decision criteria we discussed:
1) Latency SLO (p95) — determines whether hosted multi-tenant can meet p95 consistently or whether reserved Dedicated GPUs are needed.
2) Throughput / burst — sustained 400–500 rps may make Dedicated more cost-effective and predictable.
3) Isolation & compliance — if procurement requires network isolation, Private VPC is possible but adds onboarding time.

Attached: redwood-deployment-comparison.pdf — short matrix comparing Hosted / Dedicated / Private with typical latency/throughput tradeoffs and recommended starting points.

Suggested next steps:
- Please share a 24–72 hour sample of your traffic (timestamps + rps by minute) — I’ve attached a CSV template.
- I’ll loop in Rishi (SE) for a technical deep dive to validate p95 projections and sizing.
- Proposed 60-min technical call the week of Mar 8 to align on deployment and canary plan.

Would you be able to send the traffic sample by end of this week? Once we have that we can size Dedicated boxes and confirm if Hosted API meets your p95 under expected traffic.

Thanks,

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput follow-up (internal recomm)

Marissa / Vivek,

I reviewed the 48‑hour traffic sample Alex sent. Quick notes and my recommendation:

- Observed peak sustained window ~420 rps for ~25–40 minutes. Tokenization and model size (~7B, 64 tokens) keep per-request compute moderate, but sustained peaks at ~400+/rps will increase tail latency in a multi-tenant Hosted environment during contention.
- Our Hosted API with autoscaling and smart routing can likely meet p95 <50ms for short bursts if we pre-warm and reserve capacity, but that pushes operational controls and cost — and there’s no strict isolation guarantee.
- Dedicated capacity gives predictable p95 at those sustained throughputs, simpler routing, and predictable cost via reserved GPUs. Also simplifies procurement for customers who want stronger isolation guarantees.

Recommendation: Proposal to FinTechCo should be Dedicated capacity sized for their peak (with burst headroom) and a short Hosted canary for development/QA. This reduces risk to the p95 SLA and aligns with their procurement ask.

I’ll draft an initial sizing estimate and cost delta (monthly reserved vs Hosted over expected q1 run-rate). If you want, I can join the Mar 8 deep dive to present the sizing and answer infra questions.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the traffic sample and the quick responses. After an internal review with Rishi and a sizing pass, our recommendation: start with Redwood Dedicated capacity sized to handle a sustained 500 rps baseline with 20% burst headroom (can revise after the canary). Rationale: Dedicated gives the most predictable p95 headroom for your 50ms requirement and aligns better with procurement/isolation ask.

What we’ll do next:
1) Rishi will share a short sizing + cost estimate (by Tue, Mar 4).
2) Schedule the technical deep-dive (60 minutes) the week of Mar 8 — Rishi + our infra SRE will join. Proposed slots: Mar 9 at 10:00 AM PT or Mar 10 at 9:00 AM PT. Please confirm preferred slot.
3) We’ll prepare a short canary plan for the Dedicated rollout and a fallback to Hosted if needed.
4) Procurement checklist: Priya, I’ve attached a SOC2 artifact starter and can pull the full packet once you confirm the scope.

Requested from FinTechCo before the deep-dive:
- Confirmation of preferred Mar 9 or Mar 10 slot.

- If possible, a short note on expected growth trajectory (q2/q3) — will affect capacity sizing.

If that plan looks good I’ll put the Mar 9 10:00 AM PT slot on the calendar and share the invite.
